design.data_model: Settings: outbound_limits: dict[str, str] parsed from OUTBOUND_LIMITS='openalex=day:0;github=minute:10;epo=minute:10;model:gemini=minute:0,day:0', where 0 means 'count only, no limit known' (never an invented number; the shipped defaults are only the limits the code already documents: GitHub unauthenticated search 10/min, EPO about 10 searches/min), and outbound_concurrency: dict[str,int] (default 4 per research source, 1 for epo, 3 for model:gemini, 1 for model:ollama). research_daily_limit stays as a deprecated alias that fills day:N for every research source. Outcome = StrEnum(ok, cached, capped, paused, upstream_limited, transport_error, http_error, bad_response, no_key). GateResult(outcome, status:int|None, data, retry_at:float|None). SourceResult adds reason: str (an Outcome value) beside status. Redis keys: budget:{source}:{window}:{bucket} (bucket = UTC date or minute index) with EXPIRE of two windows; rs:neg:{source} kept for pauses. Session usage becomes {'by_provider': {'gemini': {'input_tokens','output_tokens','requests'}, 'ollama': {...}}} with a reader that accepts the old flat dict (T34 owns the document version bump).
design.algorithm: gate.call(source, send): if paused(source) -> GateResult(paused). For each window of the policy: read the counter; if limit>0 and used>=limit -> capped (nothing is incremented for refused calls). Acquire the per-source semaphore; INCR each window counter; await send() inside try: httpx.TransportError -> transport_error; JSON/ValueError -> bad_response; 429 (and 403 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 for GitHub) -> pause until Retry-After or the reset header, upstream_limited; other non-2xx -> http_error(status); 2xx -> ok. Record the outcome in a per-source daily counter (outcome:{source}:{date}) for the dashboard. Mapping to SourceResult: ok->ok; capped->budget_exhausted with note 'Vanigam's own limit for <source> reached; resets <time>'; paused->budget_exhausted 'asked us to wait until <time>'; upstream_limited->budget_exhausted with the key hint only when no key is configured; transport_error/http_error/bad_response->error. Models: seat calls use gate.call('model:gemini', ..., priority='bulk'); bulk callers are refused (capped) when the minute window has fewer than reserve (default 2) left, so live turns keep headroom; seats refused by the gate fall back to the rule seat with reason 'rate', and a gate refusal is NOT a Breaker.fail (no call was made). _spent sums only metered providers. Parallelism: papers() gathers its three OpenAlex requests; scan gathers element rows; novelty gathers context and retarget; _research_work runs scan and novelty's part/pair counts concurrently and joins for the context step. Board: asyncio.Semaphore per kind (research 4, council 2 by default) acquired inside run(), so a queued job is RUNNING to wait() and the turn simply narrates 'still looking'. Before the pause check, an optional policy pre-check (registered by T25) may return POLICY; nothing is sent or counted.
design.rollout: 1) Land the gate with isolation and the outcome enum behind existing settings (research_daily_limit mapped into day windows), so behaviour is unchanged except that one failing source no longer fails the scan. 2) Switch connectors and the 429 notes to reasons; update the runbook table of reasons -> actions. 3) Add parallel calls once per-source semaphores are in place. 4) Route model providers and the panel through the gate; split usage per provider with a backward-compatible reader. 5) Expose the snapshot to the monitoring work.
design.offline: Redis off: counters and pauses live in process (as today). Network off: every call ends as transport_error, each source reports 'not searched this time', and the conversation continues on local data and the rule path. verdicts.reasoning: Both find the cause (the id is the only credential; owner is a free 'anon' string in three places; no claim, no list) and both add a nullable owner_id FK with cascade, get_optional_user, a 404-not-403 owner rule, an atomic conditional claim of several sessions with a titled confirmation, and a my-conversations list. The real disagreement is the anonymous credential. A argues a 128-bit id is enough if it stays on the device, and redacts ids in structlog. But the id sits in the URL path of every route (routers/ideation.py), so uvicorn access logs, hosting proxies and error trackers see it, which A's structlog processor does not cover; and A's claim needs only the id, so anyone who saw an id in a log can claim an anonymous conversation into their own account and lock the founder out. B's per-session key in an X-Session-Key header, stored hashed and required for claim, closes both at the cost of one column and one header. B's separate cohort_ref is superseded: both T20 designs (including B's own) replace programme session ids with join-code membership, so cohort_ref would be a dead third mechanism. Final: B's capability key and keyed claim; A's details (claim ignores the six-hour idle hide but respects retention, column-only listing with a title from JSONB, 401 on an invalid token, id redaction in our logs as defence in depth, and the T19 consent copy inside claim); no cohort_ref, with T20 owning programme access.

final.chosen: Nullable owner_id FK with cascade as the single owner; per-session capability key (hashed, sent only in X-Session-Key) for anonymous sessions and the owner's token for claimed ones, checked in one session_access dependency; atomic keyed claim of up to 20 sessions after a titled confirmation; my-conversations list; programme access handled by T20 membership, not by session ids or a cohort_ref
final.why_chosen: It closes every hole without forcing sign-up: a claimed session opens only for its owner; an anonymous one needs a secret that never appears in a path or log line; a claim needs that same secret, so a leaked id cannot be used to take a conversation; and the FK makes 'delete my account removes my conversations' true by construction. verdicts.reasoning: Both remove the root cause the same way (server-owned membership by join code and enrolment token, one disclosure function with suppression under 5, base-5 rounding and banded shares, interim per-programme operator key) and reject DP, query auditing and k-anonymity for the right reasons. Verified: cohort.py:33-40 aggregates any caller list of up to 500 ids through store.get. The difference is temporal differencing. A recomputes a snapshot once a day, so a day with exactly one join or withdrawal still lets a manager compare two days, and rounding only hides that away from boundaries; B publishes a new snapshot only when the symmetric difference of members since the last publication is 5 or more, which closes single-join differencing. A is better on storage and fit: membership lives on the session document (programme field, indexed programme_id column later) with list_by_programme, the registry is a small file with a CLI that prints codes once, and people are deduplicated by owner_id after T17's claim. B's single programme document holding a members map is a write hot spot and puts programme state in the session store. Join codes are short and low-entropy, so B's keyed HMAC (SECRET_KEY now, T30 keyring later) is the right hash rather than A's plain SHA-256. Final: A's membership model and plan with B's step-of-5 publication and HMAC hashing.

final.chosen: Server-owned membership via join codes and enrolment tokens on the session document, one disclosure function for every output, snapshots republished only after a membership change of 5 or more, keyed-HMAC hashes for join codes and operator keys, and an interim per-programme operator key (replaced by a role later)
final.why_chosen: It removes caller-chosen sets and session ids from the programme flow in one move, counts founders rather than sessions, and every number passes one deterministic rule that matches the 'bands, not rankings' promise. Step-of-5 publication closes differencing across time, which a daily snapshot alone does not. Keeping membership on the session document (with a file registry and CLI) avoids a contended programme document and works offline on the memory store before accounts exist.

Routing the refresher through the T15 gate and the relevance through T01's cues reuses shared mechanisms instead of adding new ones. design.components: 1) news/ingest.py: ingest(raw) -> RawArticle | None: drop if source_id not in BY_ID; published -> ISO via date/datetime.fromisoformat then email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime, else None ('date unknown'); _clamp moves here. 2) news/corpus.py: Corpus {provider: fixture|live, refreshed_at, sources: {id: {etag, last_modified, robots_checked_at, robots_allowed, last_status, last_ok_at}}, items}; read()/write() atomically on settings.news_corpus_file (resolved per 5.4.4.2) with a Redis copy; items kept 60 days; the fixture fetcher writes a provider=fixture corpus when none exists. 3) news/refresh.py + scripts/news_refresh.py: per fetchable source, robots via urllib.robotparser (re-read daily), conditional GET through the T15 gate (source 'news:<id>', hourly window), follow_redirects off and a manual loop of at most 3 hops checked by is_fetchable_url (https and fetchable host), feedparser in HttpNewsFetcher once D9 allows, ingest, merge by item_id; one failing source keeps its old items and records why. 4) pipeline.rank(): ingest guard first, then dedupe; classify() kind in {call, closed, funding_news, other} from phrase lists (call: 'apply by', 'last date', 'applications open', 'invites applications', 'deadline', Tamil 'விண்ணப்பிக்க', 'கடைசி நாள்'; closed: 'closed', 'ended', 'results announced', 'deadline passed'; funding_news: 'raises', 'raised', 'secures', 'Series A-E', 'funding round'); deadline reader for '20 September', 'September 20, 2026', '20/09/2026', '20.09.2026' and Tamil month names near call phrases; latest deadline < today -> closed. Relevance: ctx.sector via T01 to_sector and Sector cues over the item text; district and stage via vocab; +0.10 when item language equals ctx.language (no filter). Tie-break newest first. 5) routers/news.py reads only the corpus; response gains corpus_refreshed_at and per-source status. 6) Intel.tsx: 'Demo items, not real news' for fixture, 'Updated <time>' for live, 'stale' after 24 h; sends sector, district, stage (non-protected) and UI language from the T18 registry.
design.data_model: corpus.json as above. RawArticle.published: str | None; NewsItem gains kind and deadline (ISO|null). NewsBoardOut gains provider demo|live, corpus_refreshed_at and source_status. FounderContext.language uses T01 Language codes.
design.algorithm: Actionability: 1.0 for an open call with a future deadline, 0.6 for an open call with no date read (reason 'check the deadline'), 0 for closed, funding_news, other, or an item with an unknown published date (recency 0, reason 'date unknown'). Other ranking weights unchanged.
design.rollout: 1) Ingest guard, date normalisation, tie-break fix (works on fixtures today). 2) Item typing and the deadline reader. 3) Intel labels, founder context, T01 relevance and language boost. 4) Corpus store, refresher script and strict guards, ready for the first verified source after D9 and 4.4.1.2; feedparser added in that PR; T32 schedules the script.
design.offline: The board serves the last stored corpus labelled with its age, or the fixture demo labelled demo; no request waits on a publisher; a failed refresh keeps the last corpus.

final.tests: Unit: rank() with an item from source 'unknown' plus a near-duplicate -> no exception, unknown absent; property test that rank() never raises; 'Fri, 17 Oct 2026 08:00:00 GMT' -> 2026-10-17 and a '48 hours' reason; garbage date -> 'date unknown', not actionable; 'raises Rs 50 crore in Series B funding' -> funding_news; 'Applications for TANSEED closed on 20 September' -> closed; 'apply by 30 November 2026' (today 2026-10-17) -> actionable; an 'agri' founder sees agritech stories via T01 cues; language boost reorders equal items; newest-first tie-break. Refresher with httpx.MockTransport: 304 keeps items; redirect to a listed non-fetchable host or to http refused; robots disallow skips the source with status; one source timing out keeps the others. Router: zero fetch calls per request; no fetchable source -> provider demo and Intel shows the demo label.
final.risks: Phrase lists miss unusual wording (false negatives are safer than a false 'act on'; the coverage test grows with harvested items). A stale corpus could show old calls; past-deadline demotion and the age label mitigate. The stdlib robots parser lacks some wildcard extensions (switch to protego only if a source needs it). The refresher depends on T32's runner; the script can be run by hand until then.
